stories.headline: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot
stories.dek: BBC reporting describes a pilot's account of a cockpit attack; DW reports that the UAE opened an investigation.
tldr: A Flydubai pilot described an attack by a co-pilot in the cockpit.
DW reported that the UAE launched a hijacking and terrorism investigation.
The collected reports do not establish an investigative finding or final account of the incident.

body.text: The BBC headline reports the pilot's account of a co-pilot attack in the cockpit. DW separately reports that the UAE opened a hijacking and terrorism investigation.

stories.whyItMatters: The case combines an aviation-security investigation with a consequential account from the flight crew. The available reporting records allegations and an inquiry, not a final determination.

stories.headline: North and South Korea trade accusations over landmines that injured three soldiers
stories.dek: A landmine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers has prompted competing claims and a demand from Seoul for an apology.
tldr: South Korea says a landmine blast injured three soldiers near the border.
Seoul called on North Korea to apologize; North Korea denied involvement, according to The Guardian.
The incident adds to tensions while diplomatic communication channels between the two Koreas remain absent, The Guardian reports.

body.text: DW reports that North and South Korea exchanged accusations after landmines injured three soldiers. The Guardian says Seoul demanded an apology and described a joint investigation that identified a live North Korean mine south of the military demarcation line.

The Guardian reports that North Korea denied involvement. The cause and responsibility therefore remain disputed in the reporting, despite the investigation findings described by Seoul and the UN Command.

stories.whyItMatters: The blast has both security and diplomatic implications: it touches a heavily militarized border and comes amid efforts to reopen channels between the two governments. Attribution remains contested.
stories.editorNote: Attribution is explicitly disputed; the headline and body preserve that uncertainty.

stories.headline: How the fighting in Ethiopia spread beyond Tigray, in maps and charts
stories.dek: Coverage links reports of fighting beyond Tigray with a rupture in Ethiopia–Eritrea relations and renewed questions about mediation.
tldr: Al Jazeera mapped how fighting in Ethiopia spread beyond Tigray.
BBC reported that Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as the northern conflict escalated.
DW examined possible routes to negotiations; the collected headlines do not establish a ceasefire or mediation agreement.

body.text: Al Jazeera's report describes fighting spreading beyond Tigray. BBC separately reports that Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as the northern conflict escalated.
DW's coverage focuses on who might bring the warring sides to negotiations. Together, the reports show conflict expansion and diplomatic strain, while leaving the prospects for talks unresolved.

stories.whyItMatters: The combination of conflict spreading and a breakdown in neighboring-state relations raises the regional stakes. The available reports point to mediation as an open question, not an agreed process.
stories.editorNote: Related coverage is grouped around the same northern Ethiopia conflict; no unreported battlefield detail is added.

tldr: Renee Good's family sued Trump administration officials over her fatal shooting by an ICE agent.
BBC and DW both report the lawsuit.
The collected coverage reports the filing; it does not resolve the claims in court.
